mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when the trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand with pockets of housing strength, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) while the unemployment rate remains below 5% indicates a supply-side shock without labor market slack, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: supply shock in tight labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% during a recession (defined as two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth proxied by GDPC1) signals an aggressive easing cycle, which typically supports equity valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND GDPC1 quarterly change < 0 for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the trigger is met, or positive returns occur in fewer than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 2% in Retail Sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average signals robust consumer demand growth, which typically boosts corporate earnings and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA by at least 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the trigger is met, or positive returns occur in fewer than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% after three months of contraction signals a labor market recovery, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 0.0% for 3 months, then > 0.5% in the next month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive following the trigger, or positive returns occur in fewer than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.8% in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) and a decline in the unemployment rate by at least 0.3 percentage points signals a synchronized improvement in supply capacity and labor market tightness, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.8% AND UNRATE monthly change <= -0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the trigger is met, or positive returns occur in fewer than 30% of triggered episodes.
